prompt: Explain urban heat islands and how cities can cool down.

card.oneLiner: Cities run hotter than their surroundings because of concrete, traffic and lost greenery, and trees, cool roofs and water bodies help bring the temperature down.
keyPoints: Dark surfaces absorb and re-radiate heat.
Traffic and industry add waste heat.
Lost trees remove cooling shade and evaporation.
Cool roofs, shade and water features reduce risk.

framework.name: India Meteorological Department
framework.gloss: Observed urban temperature and heatwave data.

framework.name: National Disaster Management Authority
framework.gloss: Guidance for city heat action plans.

whatYouCanDo: Use light or reflective roofing where possible.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Heat patterns differ across neighbourhoods.

prompt: Explain how transport contributes to city emissions and air pollution.
hook: Tailpipes are a big slice of city air.

card.oneLiner: Road transport is a major source of urban emissions and air pollution, and public transport, walking and cycling reduce both.
keyPoints: Vehicles emit both greenhouse gases and health-harming pollutants.
Congestion wastes fuel and worsens exposure.
Public transport and active travel cut emissions per trip.
Electric buses and vehicles shift pollution away from streets.

framework.name: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
framework.gloss: National urban transport policy and programmes.

whatYouCanDo: Use public transport, cycling or walking for short trips.
Consider electric options for the next vehicle.
Support better bus services and last-mile links.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Emissions depend on fleet, fuel and distance.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain how buildings can be made energy-efficient and climate-friendly.
hook: Buildings lock in decades of energy use.

card.oneLiner: Building design, insulation and efficient systems cut energy demand for decades, and energy codes and ratings push the shift.
keyPoints: Orientation, shading and insulation reduce cooling load.
Efficient lighting and cooling cut running energy.
Cool roofs lower heat gain in hot climates.
Retrofits can upgrade existing buildings.

framework.name: Energy Conservation Building Code
framework.gloss: Codes and ratings for efficient building design.

whatYouCanDo: Use shading, ventilation and a light roof.
Consider a green-building rating for new construction.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Payback depends on climate and usage.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain why urban green spaces matter for climate and health.

card.oneLiner: Urban trees and green spaces cool cities, clean the air, absorb rainwater and improve physical and mental health.
keyPoints: Shade and evaporation lower local temperatures.
Vegetation traps some pollutants and absorbs rain.
Green spaces support birds, insects and people.
Benefits are often greater in denser neighbourhoods.

framework.name: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
framework.gloss: Guidance on urban green spaces and planning.

framework.name: World Health Organization
framework.gloss: Evidence on green space and health.

whatYouCanDo: Care for street trees in your area.
Create community gardens and pocket parks.
Protect existing green areas from construction.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Access to green space is uneven.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain how heat and pollution affect public health in Indian cities.
hook: Climate change is a health story.

card.oneLiner: Heatwaves and air pollution raise illness and death, and heat action plans and clean-air measures protect the most vulnerable.
keyPoints: Heat stress causes dehydration, stroke and death.
Outdoor workers and the elderly are most at risk.
Air pollution worsens respiratory and heart disease.
Vulnerable groups include children and the poor.

framework.name: Ministry of Health & Family Welfare
framework.gloss: National health policy and heat-health advisories.

framework.name: World Health Organization
framework.gloss: Evidence on heat, air pollution and health.

whatYouCanDo: Follow local heat advisories and stay hydrated.
Provide shade and water for outdoor workers.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. In a health emergency, contact medical services.
